guide.title: A practical guide to getting started
guide.subtitle: Follow the basics from registration to creating documents and reviewing reports. This guide is an introduction, not a substitute for advice from your accounting professional.
guide.importantTitle: Important about accounting and tax data
guide.importantText: Check source documents, account classifications and current tax requirements before recording or filing. Reports help organize information; they do not certify its accuracy or guarantee automatic filing for every tax type.

sections.title: Create an account and company
sections.intro: Start with a trial account to explore the system before choosing how to continue.
steps: Register with your user details and company name. The trial is 14 days for one user.
Sign in and review your company details before creating documents.
When the trial ends, contact the team to ask about continued access.

sections.title: Prepare basic company records
sections.intro: Company and contact details help keep the documents you create complete.
steps: Review your company name, address and tax ID in company settings.
Add customers and suppliers to your contacts.
If you sell products, review product names, prices and opening stock before using inventory.

sections.title: Create sales documents and record payments
sections.intro: Use quotations and invoices to record sales, then enter payments based on the supporting evidence.
steps: Create a quotation, select a customer and add products or services.
Review the document details and totals before saving.
Create an invoice for the sale, record the payment and issue a receipt through the relevant workflow.

sections.title: Record expenses and keep evidence
sections.intro: Record expenses from the original documents so entries can be reviewed later.
steps: Read the receipt or tax invoice before entering its amount, date and details.
Choose a category that matches the transaction and attach evidence where supported.
Check the amount, VAT and withholding tax against the source document before saving.

sections.title: Review reports and tax information
sections.intro: Use reports to review recorded entries, not as a substitute for source documents or professional advice.
steps: Choose a period in the profit and loss or cash flow report.
Compare report totals with source documents and actual receipts or payments.
Use tax reports as preparation data, and check current requirements before filing.
sections.note: Profit may be calculated on an accrual basis, while cash flow represents cash received and paid. Read each report according to its purpose.

sections.title: Use optional modules and manage access
sections.intro: Some capabilities are optional modules and may need to be enabled or connected first.
steps: Ask your administrator to confirm that the company has enabled the module you need.
Available application areas include POS, branches, members, food service, promotions, and e-commerce or delivery integrations.
Ask an administrator to assign appropriate access before inviting team members to work.
sections.note: Stock is not synchronized across branches in real time, and multi-currency operations are not supported.

faq.title: Questions about MBSuite?
faq.subtitle: Quick answers about the platform, deployment and licensing.

items.q: Does MBSuite support Thai accounting and tax workflows?
items.a: MBSuite provides reports and tax summaries from recorded entries, and can send some data through the RD API after configuration. Review the data and current requirements before filing; the system does not guarantee automated filing for every tax type.

items.q: Does it include AI tools for accounting?
items.a: AI Chat can help answer questions, and AI Audit can flag entries for review. Treat the results as supporting information, not professional advice or confirmation that accounting records are correct.

items.q: Do I need an annual subscription?
items.a: No. In addition to an annual subscription, perpetual licensing is available. Contact our team for details.

items.q: Can I install the system myself?
items.a: Docker deployment is available for self-hosting and requires a configured database and application environment. Subscription users can start by registering and creating a company.

items.q: How does Google Drive backup work?
items.a: A company administrator must connect the company's Google Drive account and configure the relevant backup or automation first. MBSuite will not send files to Drive until it is connected.

items.q: Can I enable only selected modules?
items.a: Yes. Optional modules include POS, inventory, CRM and loyalty, branches, food service, promotions, e-commerce and delivery. Some integrations require configuration.

items.q: Does MBSuite support multiple currencies or real-time stock across branches?
items.a: Multi-currency operations are not supported, and branch stock does not synchronize in real time. Check this fit before choosing MBSuite if either is essential.
